scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: five plus three is fifty three
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The user types five, then three. Our program prints fifty three, not eight. Why? Input gives strings. Plus joins strings. So the text five and the text three are joined. Wrap each answer in int, and Python adds the numbers. We look at int in four episodes.

props.wrongCode:
a = input("First: ")
b = input("Second: ")
print(a + b)
props.fixedCode:
a = input("First: ")
b = input("Second: ")
print(int(a) + int(b))
props.why: input always returns a string, and plus joins strings, so the digits are joined instead of added; int() turns them into numbers first.

shorts.title: Make your program listen
shorts.script: Until now your program only talked. The input function lets it listen. It shows a question on the screen, then waits. You type an answer and press Enter. Python gives the answer back, and you save it in a name. Name equals input, open bracket, your question in quotes, close bracket. That is how every quiz and every form begins. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Make your program listen.

shorts.title: Input is always text
shorts.script: Here is the surprise about input. Whatever the user types comes back as a string. Even if they type a number, you get the characters of that number, as text. Type four two, and you get the string four two, not the number. So you cannot do maths with it yet. First convert it. You learn how very soon. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Typed numbers are text.

shorts.title: Use the answer
shorts.script: Look at this program. Name equals input, your name question. Then print, hello, comma, name. The answer from the user is tied to a name, so you can use it anywhere below. Ask once, use many times. You can even ask two questions, save both answers, and print them in one sentence. Try it with your own name. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Ask once, use many times.

shorts.title: Five plus three is fifty three
shorts.script: A famous beginner bug. The user types five and three, and your program prints fifty three. Why? Input gives strings, and plus joins strings. So the text five and the text three are joined into fifty three. The fix is to wrap each answer in int, so Python adds numbers instead. Always convert before you do maths. Then run it, and compare with what you predicted. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Input gives strings.
